skills_considered.reason: The operator supplied a complete local PMC XML; retrieval was needed only for linked figure and supplementary surfaces.
The operator fixed this paper as the second sequential read, so queue reprioritisation could not change the cursor.
Scientific ledgers are canonical and append-only; without BATCH_COMMIT the result lands in a dossier and commit candidate.
The overexpression cancer study bounds mechanisms but does not justify a new disease intervention hypothesis.
No compound, dose, treatment window or patient-facing intervention is evaluated in this paper.
BLOCK_BATCH_COMMIT remains explicit and the four canonical scientific current files were not edited.

group_assessment.weighting: The Aqeilan laboratory is a high-volume primary WWOX group. This increases confidence in construct and pathway context but not external replication. Same-group continuity is useful for the WWOX–DVL2 and miR-146a programs, while forced-expression designs, model identity and supplementary inconsistencies are weighted directly rather than uplifted by authorship.

field_density.note: Broad full-text counts are dense for metastasis and Wnt but include secondary mentions. Direct miR-146a and DVL2 intersections are smaller; this study is mechanistically relevant but remains largely same-lab and cell-line based.

multihop.note: All 62 references were enumerated sequentially. PMID 19465938 is the prior WWOX-DVL interaction anchor; other cited pathway work supplies context but is not upgraded by this read.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where do WWOX-DVL2/Wnt and miR-146a mechanisms already occur, and what new evidence or boundary does PMID 32300104 add?
corpus_crossquery.note: Post-reading audit found CORPUS-STUB-050 plus existing DVL2/Wnt and interactome discovery records. This paper adds SMAD3 3'UTR evidence and same-lab contextual support for DVL2, while its supplementary β-catenin ratio and cross-model transfer limit promotion strength.

retraction_check.result: Repository and indexed-record checks on 2026-08-10 returned no retraction, expression of concern or correction for PMID 32300104.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: The local PMC JATS artifact identifies PMCID PMC7162874, PMID 32300104 and a complete body, figures, methods and 62-reference list; all cited surfaces are fingerprinted.

entries.proposition: The discovery transcriptome used MDA-MB435S metastatic melanoma cells, not a breast-cancer line.
entries.snippet: we performed mRNA profiling of MDA-MB435S metastatic melanoma cells expressing an empty-vector (EV), WWOX and a WWOX-WFPA mutant

entries.proposition: The Results report 833 downregulated and 724 upregulated genes.
entries.snippet: we found 833 downregulated genes and 724 upregulated genes

entries.proposition: The stated transcriptomic significance rule required fourfold change and FDR below 0.05.
entries.snippet: Genes with a four-fold expression difference and cutoff FDR < 0.05 (by the Beonferroni method) were designated as significant.

entries.proposition: The integrated miRNA targets were computational predictions rather than generally validated targets.
entries.snippet: we performed miRNA consensus target prediction analysis by employing miRWalk (v.2.0) tool

entries.proposition: Mutation of the SMAD3 3'UTR abolished miR-146a repression.
entries.snippet: This repression was abolished upon mutating the 3′UTR

entries.proposition: The WWOX IP-MS experiment used three biological replicates.
entries.snippet: IP-MS was preformed using three biological replicates.

entries.proposition: WWOX-DVL2 association was validated by exogenous co-IP and increased with Wnt ligand.
entries.snippet: physical interaction between WWOX and DVL2 was evident even without Wnt ligands. Addition of Wnt ligands to the cells further enhanced the binding between WWOX and DVL2

entries.proposition: The therapeutic conclusion is prospective rather than experimentally tested.
entries.snippet: We conclude that therapeutic introduction of WWOX expression in early and late stages of carcinogenesis could have beneficial outcomes for cancer intervention.

entries.proposition: The Figure 1 caption assigns WWOX blue and WFPA green in the clustering panel.
entries.snippet: Of these, two clusters included genes that were strongly upregulated or downregulated in WWOX (blue) cells compared to EV (red) or WFPA (green) cells.
entries.anchor: Figure 1A caption, text half of the caption/pixel colour contradiction

entries.proposition: Figure 1's caption swaps the plotted WWOX and WFPA colour identities.
entries.snippet: The PCA pixels label EV red, WWOX green and WFPA blue; the caption instead assigns WWOX blue and WFPA green.

entries.proposition: The anti-miR-146a experiment gives partial rather than full SMAD3 rescue.
entries.snippet: Panel D densitometry shows SMAD3 near 1.00 in EV, 0.40 in WWOX plus control anti-miR, and 0.66 after anti-miR-146a.
entries.anchor: Figure 4D, inspected at native pixels after 96-effective-PPI preflight

entries.proposition: Wild-type WWOX lowers the Wnt target AXIN2 whereas the WW1 mutant does not reproduce that effect.
entries.snippet: Panels C and E show lower AXIN2 with wild-type WWOX in MDA-MB231 and SUM149 cells, while the WFPA arm in SUM149 remains near EV.

entries.proposition: The supplementary nuclear beta-catenin metric is coupled to the WWOX intervention through its denominator.
entries.snippet: Supplementary Figure S2 labels the reported densitometry β-catenin/WWOX ratio even though WWOX is the manipulated protein; Lamin is displayed but not used as the denominator.
